item.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.19037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,\Phi)$ with $(E,\Phi)\cong(E,-\Phi)$. For a complex reductive group $G$ realized as a self-adjoint subgroup of $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, we show that if $(E,\Phi)$ corresponds to a representation $\rho$ of $\pi_1(\Sigma)$, then $(E,-\Phi)$ corresponds to $(\overline{\rho}^{\,t})^{-1}$. As a consequence, the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles is the fixed locus of an involution of the character variety and carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. For a connected semisimple group and every topological type, we prove that the reversible locus in the smooth moduli space is a $(B,A,A)$-brane. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $\eta\mapsto-\eta$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.
item.dc:creator: Krishnendu Gongopadhyay, Tathagata Nayak

item.title: Remarks on Lattice Actions Corresponding to Automorphism Groups of Smooth Cubic Fourfolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.19161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The automorphism groups of smooth cubic fourfolds over the complex numbers, together with actions on defining equations, are classified in previous works. In this paper, we complete the calculation of group actions on the primitive integral cohomology lattice for all of the $156$ families in the classification. We distinguish similar families, determine the remaining action-maximal cases, and use restriction to complete the list. We also determine the generic algebraic lattices for each family. The calculation depends mainly on OSCAR.jl.
item.dc:creator: Jie Fu

item.title: On the Arnold corank, the Zariski multiplicity, and the tangent Milnor fiber problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.19357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we approach the Arnold corank problem posed by Arnold himself in 1975, which asks whether the corank of a holomorphic function is a topological invariant. Here, the corank of a holomorphic function is the corank of its Hessian matrix at 0, which is one of the most basic and fundamental invariants of a holomorphic function. Here, we prove the topological invariance of the corank mod 2. Consequently, we obtain another proof of the Arnold corank problem in dimension 3, which was recently proved by Fernandes, Jelonek, and the author of this article. We also prove that the corank is constant in a continuous family of holomorphic functions with isolated singularities and constant Milnor number. We also approach a conjecture recently posed by Budur, Fern\'andez de Bobadilla, L\^e, and Nguyen (2022), which states that if two germs of holomorphic functions are right topologically equivalent, then the Milnor fibers of their initial forms are homotopy equivalent. We prove that a (much) weaker version of this conjecture, which states that if two holomorphic functions are right topologically equivalent, then the Milnor fibers of their initial forms have the same Euler characteristic, is equivalent to the Zariski multiplicity conjecture for right topological equivalence. Some other results are also presented here. For instance, the multiplicity $> 2$ of generalized semi-Bireskorn-Pham hypersurfaces is an invariant for the right topological equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Edson Sampaio

item.title: Birational maps of moduli spaces of stable sheaves on a K3 surface induced by Fourier-Mukai transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.19437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We shall study birational maps of moduli spaces of stable sheaves on a K3 surface with Picard number 1 induced by Fourier-Mukai transforms.
item.dc:creator: Kota Yoshioka

item.title: Fourier-Mukai transforms by a family of stable sheaves and preservation of stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.19449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a Fourier-Mukai transform whose kernel is a family of Gieseker stable sheaves, we shall give a condition for the preservation of Gieseker stability of sheaves.
item.dc:creator: Kota Yoshioka

item.title: Algebraically Integrable Smooth Convex Bodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.19660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a convex body with $C^\infty$ boundary in an odd dimension $n\ge3$ is algebraically integrable if and only if it is an ellipsoid. This answers Arnold's problem for smooth convex bodies. Together with Vassiliev's even-dimensional nonexistence theorem, it gives the classification in every dimension $n\ge2$. More generally, in odd dimensions, a convex body with $C^\infty$ semialgebraic boundary is an ellipsoid whenever its section volume function satisfies a joint algebraic relation.
item.dc:creator: Junjie Shan

item.title: Maximum Likelihood Degrees via One-Edge Chordal Completion
item.description: arXiv:2610.19669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The maximum likelihood degree of a Gaussian graphical model measures the algebraic complexity of its likelihood equations. This paper studies maximum likelihood degrees of Gaussian graphical models through chordal completion. When a graph becomes chordal after one missing edge is added, its maximum likelihood degree is determined by the maximal cliques and clique-tree separators containing that edge. This recovers Uhler's formula for complete bipartite graphs with one part of size two, and extends it to deleted-spine clique books, whose degree is unchanged when a page is thickened to a clique. For several fill edges, the same method gives a product formula when no clique or separator bag contains two fill edges. We also determine four classes of vertices at which clique blow-up preserves the degree. Two follow from known results, and two are established here.
item.dc:creator: Nilava Metya

item.title: The regular inverse Galois problem over fields avoiding a curve
item.description: arXiv:2610.19689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k_0$ be a field of characteristic $0$, and let $C/k_0$ be a smooth geometrically integral curve of positive genus with $C(k_0)=\varnothing$. We prove that the regular inverse Galois problem is solvable over every field existentially closed in the class of $k_0$-fields avoiding $C$, including the curve-excluding fields of Johnson and the author. To this end, we show that for every finite group $G$, there is a parameter variety over $\mathbb Q$ whose function field admits a regular realization of $G$ without adding points to $C$. Finally, we establish $\mathrm{RIGP}$ over the variety-excluding fields of Szachniewicz and the author, when the excluded variety is a locally closed subvariety of an abelian variety.
item.dc:creator: Jinhe Ye

item.title: The volume of foliated surfaces with geometric genus one
item.description: arXiv:2610.19788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the sharp volume bound $\mathrm{vol}(\mathcal{F})\ge 1/6$ for complex foliated surfaces of general type with positive geometric genus. We also study the equality case and apply the bound to the algebraic integrability and finiteness of small volumes on irregular surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Zhiming Guo, Bokai Hu, Xin L\"u

item.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures III: Unfoldings
item.description: arXiv:2610.20011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves. We prove theorem of existence for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves for one-parameter families. We prove theorem of completeness for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves. We also present unfoldings of foliated nonsingular varieties defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves in the language of functors of Artin rings which is the algebraic version of unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures. We identify first-order unfoldings and obstructions.
item.dc:creator: Chunghoon Kim

item.title: On the Topology of Fibers of Rational Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.20025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1988 Broughton proved that if a complex polynomial function on ${\mathbb C}^n$ is tame at infinity its fibers are homotopy equivalent to bouquets of some spheres. Since then several basic properties of polynomial functions were studied by many mathematicians in various situations. In this paper, we show some evidence for the possibility of extending Broughton's result to rational functions satisfying some tameness condition at infinity and the one at their points of indeterminacy. Specifically, assuming some conditions on a rational function on ${\mathbb C}^n$ we prove that the cohomology groups of a generic fiber of it are isomorphic to those of a bouquet of $S^1$ and some spheres. In the course of the proof, the theory of the nearby and vanishing cycle sheaves for meromorphic functions will play an essential role.
item.dc:creator: Kiyoshi Takeuchi

item.title: Markman--Markushevich principle and Lagrangian fibrations on O'Grady six-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.20044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To any compact holomorphically symplectic manifold and a nef BBF-isotropic class we associate a quasi-projective variety called the Markman--Markushevich space which parametrises the Lagrangian fibrations with this isotropic class modulo Tate--Shafarevich twists. We give a systematic interpretation of known results about Tate--Shafarevich twists of Lagrangian fibrations using this space, employ it to obtain a conjectural result for the last deformation type for which such a result is not yet proposed, and make some first steps towards its proof. As a byproduct, we generalise the results of Kumar on existence Shioda--Inose partners for abelian surfaces to a slightly more general class of K3 surfaces, and associate a canonical K3 surface with transcendental lattice isometric to $U^2\oplus\langle-2\rangle^2$ to a smooth cubic surface with a choice of a Schl\"afli double-six. We also review some other approaches towards the construction of complete families of O'Grady six-manifolds with Lagrangian fibrations, and show how they may still be useful even though they do not quite work.
item.dc:creator: Rodion D\'eev

item.title: Uniform non-homogeneous vector bundles: A counterexample to the conjecture of Dr\'ezet and Ballico-Ellia
item.description: arXiv:2610.20208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a rank-9 uniform non-homogeneous vector bundle on ${\mathbb P}^5$. This yields the first counterexample to the longstanding open conjecture that every uniform vector bundle of rank $r<2n$ on ${\mathbb P}^n$ is homogeneous.
item.dc:creator: Graham Denham, Rosa Mir\'o-Roig, Hal Schenck

item.title: $\chi$-Independence for BPS Invariants of Warped Local Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.20212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A well-known conjecture of Toda's asserts that the BPS invariants associated to a Calabi--Yau threefold are independent of the chosen Euler characteristic. We answer the question in the affirmative for a certain class of local surfaces, which we call warped local curves. Along the way we show that the moduli stack of sheaves on a warped local curve can be written as the global critical locus of a function. We also show that the moduli stack of sheaves on a curve fibration over $\mathbb{A}^1$ is the global critical locus of a function.
item.dc:creator: Ana Pavlakovi\'c

item.title: Stable atomic vector bundles are 1-obstructed
item.description: arXiv:2610.20213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every stable atomic (twisted) vector bundle on a projective hyper-K\"ahler manifold is 1-obstructed. In the appendix, we construct a simple atomic object that is not 1-obstructed, providing a counterexample to Beckmann's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Hanfei Guo

item.title: Chow groups of symmetric products of projective space
item.description: arXiv:2610.20239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the integral cycle class map for $\SP^d(\PP^n)$ is split injective, with finite cokernel annihilated by $d!$,and we determine the ranks of Chow groups for $\mathrm{SP}^d(\mathbb{P}^n)$. Compatible integral transfer retractions show that $\CH_q(\SP^d(\PP^n))$ stabilizes for $d\geq q$. An explicit nonalgebraic order two class persists under addition of points, producing a split cokernel summand even in the range $q\leq d$ and in the infinite symmetric product. For the smooth configuration open set, we identify the codimension two cokernel with third unramified cohomology and detect its ramification on a rational resolution. In contrast to addition, even multiplicities annihilate a nonzero Chow class.
item.dc:creator: Youming Chen, Wenchuan Hu

item.title: On the Structure of Radical Towers and their Parametrizations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radical parametrizations describe algebraic varieties by means of nested radicals of polynomials, and their theory relies on three varieties associated with a parametrization, namely, the incidence, tower and radical varieties. In this paper we revisit this framework from a computational point of view and show that it is governed by the radical tower rather than by the particular parametrization. We prove that the tower variety depends only on the tower and that the incidence variety is always irreducible, so that no prime decomposition is needed. Moreover, we show how to replace a tower by an isomorphic one whose tower variety is defined by the equations of the tower, so that it can be computed without elimination. We introduce universal radical parametrizations and we use them to settle, under a natural hypothesis on the coefficients, an open case in the transformation of differential equations with radical coefficients into equations with rational coefficients. We show that radical subtowers form a lattice, which yields minimal radical parametrizations, and we give algorithms to compute them. We also prove that dominance between towers induces a unique dominant rational map between their tower varieties, through which unirationality is transferred. Finally, we study towers over subfields of $\mathbb{C}$ and, in the real case, relate the real points of the tower variety to the real domains of the associated parametrizations.
item.dc:creator: Javier Sendra-Arranz, Juan Rafael Sendra, Juana Sendra

item.title: Deformations of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the notion of holomorphic $p$-contact structure, that we introduced recently in the scalar case with H. Kasuya and L. Ugarte and in the line-bundle case with K. Broder, in the context of a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds equipped with a holomorphic family of holomorphic line bundles. Firstly, we show that the existence of a holomorphic $p$-contact structure is {\bf deformation-open} when a non-jumping assumption is made on the $\bar\partial$-cohomology of bidegree $(p,\,0)$. This ought to become a source of further examples of holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds. Secondly, we obtain a Berndtsson-type {\bf (semi-)positivity} result for the holomorphic vector bundle over the base induced, as a direct image, by the line bundle on the total space that supports the p-contact structures. Thirdly, we introduce a moduli space of relative holomorphic p-contact structures and we show that it is {\bf Hausdorff} and {\bf open} in a certain quotient topological space.
item.dc:creator: Dan Popovici

item.title: A prismatic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2610.20466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the category of constructible $p$-Kummer-\'{e}tale sheaves on the log adic generic fiber $(\mathrm{X},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{D}})_\eta$ for the stratification induced by a horizontal normal crossings divisor $\mathrm{D}$, showing that it is antiequivalent to a category of finitely generated unit Laurent crystals on the log prismatic site. We give a local description of finitely generated unit crystals on a framed log affine in terms of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules, and show pushforward compatibility for strict log smooth proper morphisms.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Pentland

item.title: Smoothness criterion for Fano orbifolds and bases of Lagrangian fibrations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a smoothness criterion for Fano varieties with quotient singularities. As an application, we show that if $X\to B$ is a Lagrangian fibration from a compact hyper-K\"ahler manifold and $B$ has quotient singularities, then $B$ is a projective space.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyu Liu

item.title: An algebro-geometric approach to profinite iterated monodromy groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.19117v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We carefully construct the profinite iterated monodromy group of a rational map as a quotient of the \'etale fundamental group of the punctured projective line. In doing so, we prove a number of folklore results regarding profinite IMGs; in particular, their topological generation by inertia concentrated in the post-critical orbit, and their relationship with the discrete iterated monodromy group over $\mathbb{C}$.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Tedeschi

item.title: Arithmetic Visibility in Polygons: Curved Sight in the Art Gallery
item.description: arXiv:2610.19506v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the classical art gallery problem, a guard sees a target when the segment joining them lies entirely within the polygon. We explore what changes when sight may bend along regular arcs on absolutely irreducible curves, but only those defined by primitive integer polynomials of total degree at most \(d\) and coefficient height at most \(H\). We call such curves admissible sight carriers. Arcs can dramatically improve sight. In a one-sided comb, no straight-line guard sees selected targets in two different teeth, yet a single central guard sees a chosen target in every tooth along parabolic carriers. Sight can also fail in two different ways. Geometrically, the polygon may block every sight arc of the allowed degree between two points. For instance, in an alternating comb, the number of guards needed for a row of targets spanning the comb grows linearly with the number of sides at each fixed degree, even for carriers with arbitrary real coefficients. Arithmetically, no admissible carrier may pass through the points at all. Even in the unit square, at fixed \(d\) and \(H\), the proportion of rational targets that must guard themselves tends to one as the height bound grows. An algebraic target may lie on no rational curve of degree at most \(d\), however large \(H\) is. Both failures can be overcome for finite target sets by allowing the degree and coefficient height to grow. We show that every finite set of algebraic targets in a rational polygon becomes visible from any rational interior guard, with explicit bounds. We also construct, for every \(d\), arbitrarily large Galois orbits in the unit square, all of projective height \(4^{d+1}\), whose points must each guard themselves at degree \(d\) for every \(H\). Yet at degree \(d+1\) and coefficient height one, a single guard sees the whole orbit along \(Z(Y-X^{d+1})\).
item.dc:creator: Malik Barrett

item.title: Gaudin from Cherednik
item.description: arXiv:2610.20146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $W$ be a complex reflection group and $X$ the De Concini-Procesi wonderful model of its reflection arrangement. Inside Etingof's sheaf of Cherednik algebras on $X$ we define a subsheaf generated by the Dunkl operators that extend the standard ones on the hyperplane complement. We conjecture that at $t=0$ the image of the logarithmic vector fields in a natural module over this subsheaf is the sheaf of Gaudin algebras on $X$ defined by Aguirre, extending a construction of Bonnaf\'e and Rouquier from the hyperplane complement to $X$. We prove the conjecture for $W=S_{3}$.
item.dc:creator: Matthew McMillan

item.title: The parity module of a matroid
item.description: arXiv:2610.20234v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the parity module of a matroid with coefficients in a field $\mathbb{k}$. When $\mathbb{k}$ has characteristic zero, we show that the parity module of a matroid is isomorphic to its intersection cohomology module, yielding a new intrinsic characterization of the latter. The structure and dimension of the parity module can vary depending on the characteristic, giving rise to characteristic-dependent generalizations of the Kazhdan-Lusztig and Z-polynomials of matroids. When the matroid is realizable over the complex numbers, the parity module is isomorphic to the hypercohomology of the parity sheaf supported on the arrangement Schubert variety of any such realization. We also introduce the notion of pure modules over any field $\mathbb{k}$ and show that they satisfy a matroid analogue of the Beilinson-Bernstein-Deligne-Gabber decomposition theorem: Every pure module over the graded M\"obius algebra decomposes as a direct sum of shifts of the parity modules of matroids obtained by restricting to flats.
item.dc:creator: Tom Braden, June Huh, Jacob P. Matherne, Nicholas Proudfoot, Botong Wang

item.title: GCD and ABC inequalities for abelian varieties over function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.20379v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove two height inequalities for rational points on abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0. The first is the GCD inequality, which shows that the height with respect to a closed subscheme of an abelian variety of codimension at least 2 is much smaller than the usual height function. This can be viewed as a compact and geometric analogue of a theorem of Levin. The second is a special case of the (geometric) abc conjecture proposed by Vojta, which compares the truncated counting function and the usual counting function. This is a compact analogue of a theorem of Guo, Nguyen, Sun and Wang, and also resolves a conjecture of Buium, which was only known for traceless abelian varieties or constant abelian varieties previously. The proofs of these inequalities follow a common three-step pattern: from microscopic local estimates to local estimates, and then to global estimates. Building on the canonical Xie-Yuan heights, we control discrete counting functions by continuous integrals of Betti forms. The main new tools are uniform Nevanlinna-type estimates for families of linear entire curves on abelian varieties; combined with covering arguments based on Besicovitch theory and averaging, these handle overlaps and gaps precisely.
item.dc:creator: Guoquan Gao

item.title: Topological recursion for spin enumeration of hypermaps
item.description: arXiv:2610.20464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish topological recursion for the spin enumeration of hypermaps, or, in the dual language, spin dessins d'enfants. This problem has remarkable features distinguishing it from other applications of topological recursion to enumerative combinatorics. First, the spectral curve is elliptic rather than rational, as in most cases studied before. Second, it contains degenerate ramification points, and one has to apply a version of degenerate topological recursion. Finally, the meromorphic correlator differentials have "moving" poles on the antidiagonals between pairs of distinct arguments, and one has to adjust the loop equations to this kind of degeneracy as well. The computations involve concepts of different kinds, such as BKP integrability, Gaussian integrals, the x-y swap, and symplectic duality.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Alexandrov, Boris Bychkov, Petr Dunin-Barkowski, Maxim Kazarian, Sergey Shadrin

item.title: Arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of modular curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.20575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the full generating series arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula on the product of two modular curves, with arbitrarily singular coefficients. This is the case $\operatorname{GSpin}(2,2)$ in Kudla's program.
item.dc:creator: Ryan C. Chen, Baiqing Zhu

item.title: Kawamata boundedness for Fano threefolds and the Graded Ring Database
item.description: arXiv:2201.07178v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an effective realisation of Kawamata's famous bound for Fano 3-folds. Our result is a list of 39,550 candidate Hilbert series $P$ for Fano 3-folds satisfying the Bogomolov stability inequality. For each $P$, there may or may not be a Fano 3-fold $X$ that realises $P$, but even so we give a set of weights that we expect to be among those of a minimal generating set of the anticanonical ring of any such $X$. This provides a crude first approximation to the ongoing classification of Fano 3-folds. We explain in detail what this data means, the important nuances that current known examples reveal about it, and how it relates to a range of different classification programmes.
item.dc:creator: Gavin Brown, Alexander Kasprzyk, Miles Reid

item.title: Irreducibility of Some Quot Schemes on Nodal Curves
item.description: arXiv:2401.10528v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $C$ be an integral projective nodal curve over $\mathbb C$, of arithmetic genus $g \geqslant 2$. Let $E$ be a vector bundle on $C$ of rank $r$ and degree $e$. Let $\textrm{Quot}_{C/\mathbb C}(E,k,d)$ denote the Quot scheme of quotients of $E$ of rank $k$ and degree $d$. We show that $\textrm{Quot}_{C/\mathbb C}(E,k,d)$ is irreducible for $d \gg 0$.
item.dc:creator: Parvez Rasul

item.title: Weak del Pezzo surfaces are characterized by the existence of $2$-tilting bundles
item.description: arXiv:2510.26199v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $d\geq1$, a tilting bundle on a regular proper $d$-dimensional variety over a field is called $d$-tilting if its endomorphism algebra has global dimension $d$, the smallest possible value. We prove that, over any field, the existence of a $d$-tilting bundle implies that the anticanonical bundle is semiample and big, and hence the variety is weak Fano. Moreover, the endomorphism algebra is $d$-representation tame. Conversely, every weak del Pezzo surface over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic admits a $2$-tilting bundle. Thus a smooth projective surface over such a field admits a $2$-tilting bundle if and only if it is a weak del Pezzo surface. This proves the variety case of Chan's conjecture, originally formulated in characteristic zero, and extends it to arbitrary characteristic. As an application, we construct a non-commutative crepant resolution (NCCR) of the anticanonical ring of any regular proper $d$-dimensional variety over any field admitting a $d$-tilting bundle. The NCCR is the endomorphism algebra of the pulled-back bundle on the total space of the canonical bundle. In particular, we obtain NCCRs of anticanonical cones over Du Val del Pezzo surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. These NCCRs are the $3$-Calabi--Yau completions of the endomorphism algebras of $2$-tilting bundles on the minimal resolutions, extending the known construction for smooth del Pezzo surfaces to the Du Val case.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Tomonaga

item.title: Cluster algebra and quasimap quantum cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2511.09875v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We apply the abelianization technique to obtain an explicit ring presentation for the quasimap quantum cohomology of GIT quotients. As an application, for quiver varieties associated with oriented-acyclic quivers, we establish a cluster algebra structure on their equivariant quasimap quantum cohomology rings.
item.dc:creator: Yingchun Zhang, Zijun Zhou

item.title: On the Hilbert-Chow crepant resolution conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2601.03036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the Hilbert-Chow crepant resolution conjecture in the exceptional curve classes for all projective surfaces and all genera. In particular, this confirms Ruan's cohomological Hilbert-Chow crepant resolution conjecture. The proof exploits Fulton-MacPherson compactifications, reducing the conjecture to the case of the affine plane.
item.dc:creator: Denis Nesterov

item.title: A cohomological interpretation for stringy Hodge numbers
item.description: arXiv:2602.19344v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain a cohomological interpretation for Batyrev's stringy Hodge numbers in the full generality in which they are defined. In a previous paper, the second and third authors used motivic integration to define the stringy Hodge--Deligne invariant of a smooth Artin stack $\mathcal{X}$ and proved that when $\mathcal{X}$ is a crepant resolution of a variety $Y$ with log-terminal singularities, the generating function for the stringy Hodge numbers of $Y$ is equal to the stringy Hodge--Deligne invariant of $\mathcal{X}$. In this paper, we introduce a cohomology theory $H_{\mathrm{str}}^*(\mathcal{X})$ that computes the stringy Hodge--Deligne invariant of $\mathcal{X}$. Since, by previous work of the second and third authors, all varieties with log-terminal singularities admit a crepant resolution by an Artin stack, this gives a cohomological interpretation for stringy Hodge numbers of any variety with log-terminal singularities. We also show that in the special case where $\mathcal{X}$ is Deligne--Mumford, $H_{\mathrm{str}}^*(\mathcal{X})$ coincides with the orbifold cohomology of $\mathcal{X}$.
item.dc:creator: Jiahui Huang, Matthew Satriano, Jeremy Usatine

item.title: Local multiplicities for an equivariantly enriched non-transverse B\'ezout's theorem
item.description: arXiv:2604.00289v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the degree and local degree in equivariant motivic homotopy theory for the purpose of studying equivariant enumerative problems over general fields. Given a finite, tame group scheme $G$ over a field $k$ and an equivariant motivic ring spectrum $E_G$, we define the equivariant motivic degree and a corresponding local degree of a relatively $E_G$-oriented, proper, quasi-smooth morphism of $G$-schemes. We prove a local to global formula expressing the global degree as a sum of local contributions over $G$-orbits. Using these constructions, we define the Euler number of an oriented vector bundle on a quasi-smooth, proper derived stack and show that the Euler number is independent of the choice of section under appropriate hypotheses. In the presence of a finite group action, the equivariant Euler number can be computed as a sum of local equivariant degrees. As an application, we obtain an equivariantly enriched local multiplicity formula for an equivariant non-transverse B\'ezout theorem, expressing an equivariant intersection number as a sum of local equivariant degrees.
item.dc:creator: Candace Bethea, Charanya Ravi

item.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties I -klt Fano case-
item.description: arXiv:2607.25181v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the following Miyaoka-Yau inequality for any $n$-dimensional klt Fano variety $X$, possibly K-unstable, in terms of its delta invariant: \[\left(2(n+1)\widehat{c}_2(X)-n c_1(X)^2\right)\cdot c_1(X)^{n-2} \ge -n \left(1-\min\{1,\delta(X)\}\right)^2 \cdot c_1(X)^n.\] Moreover, if equality holds in this inequality, then there exist a finite quasi-\'etale cover $\widehat{X} \to X$ and a positive integer $p$ such that $\widehat{X} \cong \mathbb{P}(1,\ldots, 1, p)$. We also discuss the relationship between Donaldson's conjecture and the Miyaoka-Yau inequality.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Hisamoto, Masataka Iwai

item.title: Arithmetic hypergeometric $\mathcal {D}$-modules and exponential sums on reductive groups
item.description: arXiv:2608.00470v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a finite family of representations of a reductive group, we define a Laurent polynomial on the group. The exponential sum associated this Laurent polynomial is called a hypergeometric exponential sum. We introduce an arithmetic hypergeometric $\mathcal D$-module to study the hypergeometric exponential sum. It is an overholonomic arithmetic $\mathcal D$-module with a Frobenius structure so that the trace of the Frobenius at a rational point is the exponential sum. We prove that over the locus where the Laurent polynomial is nondegenerate, the arithmetic hypergeometric $\mathcal {D}$-module defines an $F$-isocrystal overconvergent along the degenerate locus. As an application, we get an estimation of the hypergeometric exponential sum.
item.dc:creator: Lei Fu, Xuanyou Li, Chenhan Liu

item.title: Sharp Quadratic Bounds for Anticanonical Volumes of Weak Fano Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.06845v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an explicit lower bound of optimal quadratic order for the anticanonical volume of every complex $\epsilon$-log canonical weak del Pezzo surface, with no restriction on its Picard number or its singularities. More precisely, the volume is at least $\min\{c_{exc},\epsilon^2/3032064\}$, where $c_{exc}>0$ is an explicit absolute constant. Quotients of the projective plane show that the exponent two is optimal. We also prove cubic upper bounds for the cyclic determinant mass and for the Picard number of a smooth rational log Calabi--Yau pair. We give geometric examples showing that these two auxiliary exponents are optimal in their respective settings.
item.dc:creator: Pinxian Bie

item.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersection in flag varieties
item.description: arXiv:2609.21914v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a root-theoretic localization formalism for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of flag varieties and of smooth zero loci of globally generated homogeneous vector bundles. The resulting invariants are expressed as finite sums over decorated trees whose contributions are determined by the root system of the ambient flag variety and by the torus weights of the defining bundle. We connect these computations with the Theory of Hodge Atoms of Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu via the matrix of small quantum multiplication by first Chern class. Let $X$ be a Fano fourfold with $h^{3,1}(X)=1$ arising as a hyperplane section of a suitable Fano fivefold. Its cohomology decomposes into a monodromy-fixed part and the middle vanishing cohomology. This decomposition is preserved by quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. Moreover, it acts by a scalar on the vanishing summand. We show, for the monodromy-fixed block, that (a) if every eigenvalue has algebraic multiplicity at most two and $X$ is Hodge general, then $X$ is irrational; (b) if every eigenvalue has Jordan defect at most one and $X$ is rational, then every weak factorization contains a smooth surface center whose minimal model is a projective K3 surface. Many applications are presented. Using the recently introduced quantum connection approach to irrationality, we obtain from the computations here presented the irrationality of the very general smooth complete intersection of a hyperplane and a quadric in $\operatorname{LG}(3,6)$; the very general smooth quadric section in $G_2/P_2$; and the very general smooth complete intersection of five hyperplanes and a quadric in the spinor 10-fold.
item.dc:creator: Boris Alexeev, Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, Giovane Galindo, Bogdan Georgiev, Ludmil Katzarkov, Pedro Antonio Muniz Martins

item.title: Generic Hodge and special Hodge--Witt polygons
item.description: arXiv:2610.05892v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the Hodge polygon of the generic fiber of a proper smooth $p$-adic formal scheme over $\mathcal O_C$ lies on or above the generalized Hodge--Witt polygon of its special fiber.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yang

item.title: KP integrability of non-perturbative differentials
item.description: arXiv:2412.18592v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the KP integrability of non-perturbative topological recursion, which can be considered as a formal $\hbar$-deformation of the Krichever construction of algebro-geometric solutions of the KP hierarchy. This property goes back to a 2011 conjecture of Borot and Eynard.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal de l'\'Ecole polytechnique -- Math\'ematiques, Volume 13 (2026), pp. 1607-1635
item.dc:creator: Alexander Alexandrov, Boris Bychkov, Petr Dunin-Barkowski, Maxim Kazarian, Sergey Shadrin

item.title: Non-Equivalence of Smooth and Nodal Conformal Block Functors in Logarithmic CFT
item.description: arXiv:2509.07720v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbb V$ be an $\mathbb N$-graded, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra (VOA) admitting a non-lowest generated module in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathbb V)$ (e.g., the triplet algebras $\mathcal{W}_p$ for $p\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2}$ or the even symplectic fermion VOAs $SF_d^+$ for $d\in \mathbb{Z}_+$). We prove that, unlike in the rational case, for $N\geq 4$ there is no vector bundle on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,N}$ whose fibers are the spaces of conformal blocks associated to certain $\mathbb{V}$-modules, since the dimensions of these conformal block spaces differ between smooth and nodal curves. Consequently, the sheaf of coinvariants associated to these $\mathbb V$-modules on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,N}$ is not locally free for $N\geq 4$. It also follows that, unlike in the rational case, the mode transition algebra $\mathfrak A$ introduced by Damiolini-Gibney-Krashen is not isomorphic to the end $\mathbb E=\int_{\mathbb X\in \mathrm{Mod}(\mathbb X)}\mathbb X\otimes \mathbb{X}'$ as an object of $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathbb{V}^{\otimes 2})$.
item.dc:creator: Hao Zhang

item.title: Potential semistability of Finite height Galois representations: Relative case
item.description: arXiv:2606.26043v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a $p$-adic field. We define the notion of finite height for an \'etale $\mathbb{Z}_p$-local system on a smooth affinoid adic space $\mathcal{X}$ over $K$ with semistable reduction. Using analytic prismatic $F$-crystals and purity results of Du-Liu-Moon-Shimizu (arXiv:2404.19603), we prove that if an \'etale $\mathbb{Z}_p$-local system over $\mathcal{X}$ is of finite height then its pullback along a finite \'etale cover of $\mathcal{X}$ is semistable. This answers a question of Tong Liu in the relative setting.
item.dc:creator: Kaustabh Mondal

item.title: Kodaira fibres and wrapped Floer cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2609.23884v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $F$ be a singular fibre of a relatively minimal complex elliptic fibration with smooth total space, and let $\Omega$ be a nonvanishing holomorphic two-form near $F$. We show that a small neighbourhood of $F$ is a Weinstein domain for $\mathrm{Re}\,\Omega$ whose completion is a Legendrian surgery, with cocores obtained by completing holomorphic disks transverse to the components of $F$. For every coefficient field and every multiplicative bulk class, we compute the wrapped Floer cohomology of these cocores and prove that it is concentrated in degree zero. The cocores generate, so the bulk-deformed wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of perfect modules over an explicit algebra: a multiplicative preprojective algebra of affine type for the normal crossing fibres, and a quiver algebra with relations for types $II$, $III$ and $IV$. Applications include formality of the affine plumbing dg algebras; mirrors given by resolved affine surfaces at every classical bulk class for affine D, E and types II, III, IV; and mirrors given by quotient stacks of algebraic tori at root-of-unity bulk classes for the four affine stars.
item.dc:creator: Yanki Lekili

item.title: The Artin-Davenport conjecture on cubic forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.08226v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that any integral cubic form in ten or more variables has a nontrivial integer zero. Like earlier authors on this topic, we use geometric methods to produce a zero in some cases, and the circle method in all other cases. New ingredients are required on both fronts: in the first case, bounds on the dimension of singular loci and incidence varieties, and in the second case, a stratified geometric sieve, together with stratification results for point counts over finite fields and a cube-root Hensel lifting analysis.
item.dc:creator: Dante Bonolis, Tim Browning, Jakob Glas, Victor Y. Wang

item.title: Equivariant noncommutative crepant resolutions and $G$-maximal modifying modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.11708v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $S$ be a Cohen-Macaulay normal domain containing a field $k$ with an action of a finite group $G$ with $|G|$ invertible in $k$. We prove that $G$-equivariant noncommutative crepant resolutions of $S$ induce noncommutative crepant resolutions of $S^G$ if the $G$-action is small. We also discuss similar results for equivariant maximal modification algebras. We introduce the notion of $G$-maximal modifying ($G$-MM) module, and we show that $G$-MM module over $S$ induces MM $S^G$-module in some special cases. Furthermore, we prove that Gorenstein MMAs of three-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein Cohen-Macaulay rings are derived equivalent. As an application of these results, we prove the existence of an MM module and derived equivalences of MMAs for three-dimensional terminal singularities of index two.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Hirano
